summary:
A survival-strategy game on a real NASA full-Moon photo: 3 resources, 3 actions a sol, real solar-weather science, and a loss screen that teaches.
NASA data: LIVE & CURATED
- DONKI /SEP + /CME — api.nasa.gov/DONKI: LIVE
- Full-Moon photo — GSFC_20171208_Archive_e000868: CURATED
- Apollo 12 surface — AS12-46-6832: CURATED
- LCROSS 2009 — Cabeus crater: CURATED
- OSDR search — ~1,064 radiation studies: CURATED
details:
THE GAME

Survive 14 sols on the Moon and beam 5 science transmissions to Earth

▪  3 actions per sol, 5 actions to choose from — each one costs resources

▪  3 resources: ⚡ Energy · 🥗 Food & Water · 🛡️ Radiation Shield

▪  Crew radiation is the silent clock: at 1000 the mission fails

▪  Easy / Normal / Hard — tuned with hundreds of simulated missions

Real problems the game teaches

- Crew radiation 0–1000, shield decay, flares: Astronaut career dose limits; solar storms tracked live by NASA's DONKI

- Search for ice in shadowed craters: Water ice = drink + oxygen + fuel. LCROSS proved it (2009); Artemis targets the pole

- Maintain shield = pile regolith on the dome: Regolith shielding is a real NASA concept — Moon soil is the cheapest barrier

- Every action burns Food & Water and Energy: Closed-loop life support: the ISS recovers ~98% of its water; the Moon has no deliveries

- Relax day lowers radiation uptake: Crew rest is an operational countermeasure on long missions

- Meteorite threshold before sol 11: Micrometeoroid risk drives real shielding and mission-planning math

Skills a 7–12 year old builds playing it

Trade-off thinking Every move helps one meter and hurts another. No perfect button exists.

Planning under uncertainty A meteorite with a hidden threshold forces a multi-sol plan, not reactions.

Mental math & budgets Percent bars, decay rates and costs become second nature in two missions.

Systems thinking Resources feed each other: power makes water, water protects from radiation.

Data literacy LIVE vs CURATED labels teach what a source is and why it matters.

Resilience Loss screens explain the exact math of failure — and a retry button.

How we built it

The game idea and design choices are the team's. Game code written with AI assistance and disclosed in the file metadata and in-game.
All imagery is real NASA public-domain photography or pure CSS — zero AI-generated pictures, zero NASA logos.
No voices or faces of minors anywhere in the project.

NASA data, LIVE & CURATED

If the live feed is unreachable, the game says so and badges itself CURATED. Static data is never shown as live — and nothing is invented.

EXTRA PLANETARY CHALLENGES

- Solar flares — radiation spikes; the game checks NASA's live DONKI feed for real storm science

- Micrometeorites — punches holes in your shield, repaired only with regolith runs

- Electrostatic dust — coats the panels, costs Energy until you clean them

- Cold-cracked water pipes — the 300°C swing between lunar day and night is real
